title: Tiered Fee Schedule

statement.md: An exchange charges a **marginal** tiered fee on monthly traded volume. A schedule has $t$ tiers: tier $j$ covers volume in $(a_{j-1}, a_j]$ with $a_0 = 0$ and $a_t = \infty$, and charges $r_j$ **hundredths of a basis point** per unit of notional in that tier (so a rate of 100 is 1 basis point and a rate of 10000 is 100 basis points, which is 1%).

For each query volume $V$, let $\text{part}_j$ be the part of $V$ inside tier $j$; so the fee is $\lfloor \sum_j r_j \cdot \text{part}_j / 10^{6} \rfloor$ (integer division, rounded down). All values are integers. Print one integer per query.

inputFormat: First line: $t$. Then $t - 1$ boundaries $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_{t-1}$ on one line (empty line if $t = 1$). Then one line with $t$ rates. Then $q$ and $q$ volumes (one per line).
hints: Precompute the cumulative fee at each boundary. Then each query is one binary search plus one multiplication.
The product $r_j \cdot \text{part}_j$ can reach $10^{16}$: it fits in 64 bit integers, and the sum over 50 tiers does too (about $5 \cdot 10^{17}$).

editorial.md: Marginal means each tier only applies to the part of the volume inside it. Precompute $C_j = \sum_{i \le j} r_i (a_i - a_{i-1})$. For a volume $V$ in tier $j$, the sum is $C_{j-1} + r_j (V - a_{j-1})$, then one integer division.

solutions.python:
import sys
from bisect import bisect_left


def main():
    lines = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    t = int(lines[0])
    a = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    r = list(map(int, lines[2].split()))
    q = int(lines[3])
    cum = [0]
    prev = 0
    for j in range(t - 1):
        cum.append(cum[-1] + r[j] * (a[j] - prev))
        prev = a[j]
    out = []
    for i in range(q):
        v = int(lines[4 + i])
        j = bisect_left(a, v)  # first boundary >= v: tier index
        lo = a[j - 1] if j > 0 else 0
        out.append(str((cum[j] + r[j] * (v - lo)) // 1000000))
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()
